title: dict census verification run
note: Every structure and operation fact on dict's census page as executable vectors; the border facts filed away there (the php impostor's resolution, records, serialization) are OUT of scope. Where the census names no camp for a language, that cell RECORDS its answer rather than checking it, and the answer is carried into the log as a proposed census addition.

expectation_alphabet.<any>: any result acceptable -- either the language guarantees nothing, or the census promises nothing, or the census claims nothing about that language
expectation_alphabet.<raise:*>: must refuse at runtime, by any name
expectation_alphabet.<compile-error>: the build refused the program -- for F-d4/rust and F-l9-dict/rust this is the guarantee itself

language_status.typescript: active (tsc -> node); its SPLIT PERSONALITY -- plain object and Map -- is recorded as separate probes
language_status.csharp: blocked-deliberate (no toolchain in the container; not pursued)
language_status.swift: not run (bonus language, outside the census's 11 targets)

facts.description: Value read by an EXISTING key answers the value.
Overwrite on a duplicate key: last write wins.
Delete removes the key; the membership test then answers no.

What a KEY may be. Anything hashable or equatable: python ruby js Map java kotlin csharp dart rust go cpp. Strings (and ints) only: php, and the js PLAIN OBJECT, which coerces silently so that position 1 and position "1" are the same slot -- probe a sets both and reads back the integer key, and the coercing camp answers with what the STRING key stored. Probe d asks the same of js Map, which does not coerce. Probe b shows the declared camp taking a non-string key without complaint.

Whether iteration order is promised. Insertion order guaranteed: python ruby php js Map dart kotlin. Explicitly NOT promised: rust java csharp cpp -- their cells therefore RECORD their order rather than check it, since checking a non-promise would be checking nothing. Actively RANDOMISED: go, the census's first ANTI-guarantee -- probe b iterates a ten-key map three times inside ONE process and asserts the orders DIFFER, because the only honest test of a promise of unpredictability is instability itself. Probe c is the js plain object's weird cousin: integer-like keys iterate first, in numeric order, before the rest in insertion order.

Reading a MISSING key -- the widest operation fracture in the census, four camps. Throw: python, csharp. Answer a nothing-value: ruby js/ts kotlin dart java php. Answer the ZERO VALUE plus an ok flag: go. INSERT a default and answer it: cpp's operator[], where probe a reports the value AND the map size afterwards, and the size having grown from 1 to 2 IS the insertion. cpp's .at() throws instead (probe b) and rust ships both spellings too: indexing panics, .get answers None (probe c).

Deleting while iterating. Error or undefined: python (RuntimeError), java (ConcurrentModificationException), csharp, and rust, whose borrow rules forbid it at BUILD time -- the cheapest possible refusal. Explicitly ALLOWED: go. Tolerated with caveats: ruby, php, js Map. cpp's answer is undefined (erasing invalidates the iterator), so its cell records rather than checks.

Key-equality fine print, billed here because the dict OWNS its key-matching rule. js Map keys by IDENTITY, so two objects of equal content are two different keys; python, ruby and java key by value-equality, so two equal keys are one. Probe b is the NaN corner: js Map retrieves a NaN key (SameValueZero), while in python a fresh NaN never matches the NaN already stored, so the entry is unreachable.

What `b = a` means for a dict -- inherited from list's F-l9 wholesale, and probed here because the census says the camps are identical and that is itself a claim. Share the object: python ruby java kotlin csharp dart js/ts go. Copy the value: php. Move: rust, refusing at build time. The census does not place cpp; its cell records rather than checks.
